data.name: Alice's Mom's Rescue
data.detailed_description:
Alice's Mom's Rescue is an indie puzzle / platformer game in the pure style of old school pixel art.
The Giant Raven Has Captured Alice's mother.
Help Alice save her mother through the 3 worlds and 25 levels!
Change Alice's height by jumping on the magic mushrooms to get through the tiny spaces.
But be aware that a small size will also affect Alice's physical abilities!
Solve puzzles, beware of the evil cats, birds, bats & spikes, and find the right path to victory.

reviews.review:
[h1]Overview:[/h1]
'[i]Alice's Mom's Rescue[/i]' is a short 2D side scrolling platformer putting players in the shoes of "Alice". A young girl who had to experience the unfortunate event of her mother being kidnapped by a large raven for seemingly no reason. She now has to set off on foot through 25 levels across 3 worlds in order to get her back. Frankly, if there were birds large enough to abduct an adult human, I'd be pretty scared too. The game is extremely simple with gameplay mechanics of the same nature. But even with this information, '[i]Alice's Mom's Rescue[/i]' still manages to possess flaws that make the game not so enjoyable to say the least.

[h1]Gameplay:[/h1]
Albeit as standard as they come, '[i]Alice's Mom's Rescue[/i]' [i]does[/i] have an extra feature alongside the typical platforming in the form of shrinking in size to access certain areas. The levels in the game appear linear at first but later on present different paths that the player must decide to take which is where the main issue in the game lies.  Now it's not out of the ordinary for sidescrollers to give players different paths to pick from, but in '[i]Alice's Mom's Rescue[/i]', picking a path determines whether or not you lose the level and have to restart.

Why is that you may ask? Well the thing is, the level design is sculpted in a way where if you pick the wrong path, you may find yourself in a position where you're not able to backtrack and retrace your steps, forcing you to restart. The reason why this is an issue is due to the simple fact that you aren't able to discern which paths you aren't yet supposed to take so inevitably, you're going to mess up. There aren't any checkpoint systems in the game so if you find out you went the wrong way (which will happen a lot), then you're forced to repeat the [b]entire[/b] level just to find the right path. It's trial and error to the lowest degree and that's bad level design. 

There's even a text that appears when you walk into a blocked area that requires a key that literally says "If you're stuck, go to the menu and restart the level". I'm not kidding. That's a pretty harsh punishment for an honest mistake which in normal cases, is just the player exploring the map. But in this game, scouting out the map can lead to a forced restart and believe me, having to play through the same segments over and over again is tedious as all hell. It doesn't help that spikes kill you instantly either so on top of risking messing up just by simply exploring, you also run the risk of restarting the entire level just cause you died. Checkpoints exist for a reason and it's to prevent issues exactly like this from happening.

Then comes the difficulty options which I'm honestly surprised the game even had. There's easy, normal and difficult but all it does is change the amount of starting health you have. I mean I [i]guess[/i] that technically makes the game harder but when most of the things in the game kill you in one hit, it really doesn't matter that much. Speaking of not mattering that much, the game also has a timer that records how long it takes for you to beat a level. Yeah, an actual "Best Time" feature was implemented and while it doesn't harm the game in anyway... just why?

[h1]Controls:[/h1]
As basic as a branch in a forest. '[i]Alice's Mom's Rescue[/i]' is among the thousands of primitive 2D platformers littering the [i]Steam[/i] store that consists only of platforming. There's no combat or anything and even the cute little evil cats can't be jumped on. On top of that, the only way to access the few settings the game has is by launching the game. Only there can you view such amazing settings such as volume, language (which there are surprisingly 6 of), controls (gamepad or keyboard), fullscreen mode and vertical sync. That's all and if you ask me, even that feels like a lot for a game like this.

[h1]Graphics:[/h1]
It looks like one of those flash games that you would play on a browser back when [i]Adobe Flash Player[/i] was still a thing. It's not unique at all and is easy to skim over. It guns for a pixelated style with bright colors that while pleasing to the eyes, doesn't detract from the fact that the visuals just aren't anything special and doesn't grab the eye. That being said, I have seen much, much worse.

[h1]Audio:[/h1]
Extremely lacking too. Contains the kind of sound effects you can easily get for free online and I could've sworn I've heard the same sound effects in this game from many other games I've played in the past. The music is also repetitive to listen to as it's the same short looping track that I'm confident came from the same pack of audio assets as the sound effects.

[h1]Conclusion/TL;DR:[/h1]
'[i]Alice's Mom's Rescue[/i]' is a short but flawed 2D sidescrolling platformer where you play as a little girl on a mission to save her kidnapped mother. The game on the surface looks like a cute platforming game but it has an underlying issue that is the lack of a checkpoint system. The level design is awful as merely exploring can sometimes put you in a position where you get stuck and have to restart the entire level. Later levels will inevitably force the player to constantly restart and replay the same sections just because there's no option to backtrack ensuring tedium. '[i]Alice's Mom's Rescue[/i]' just isn't great and for the price, you can find [i]far[/i] better options.
